label: Afternoon edition
summary: Keanu, **Nvidia gave back part of Monday's record rally**, falling 5.86% to $155.38 as chip stocks dropped, the Nasdaq lost 1.48% and the Dow rose 0.85% (CNBC, NBC News). Senate Banking set **Huang's testimony for Dec. 3**, and lawmakers in both parties still question the board's reinstatement (CNBC, The Hill, Fox News). Anthropic closed 6.5% below its $83 IPO price on its fourth trading day, though six of seven analysts rate it a buy (CNBC, Bloomberg). Locally, San Francisco topped its November tide record at 8.23 feet, and **the king tide peaks near 11 a.m. Wednesday** under a coastal flood warning (KQED, CNN). Prosecutors from 29 counties asked the California Supreme Court to halt Newsom's death-row commutations, and his reply is due Dec. 4 (CalMatters, CNN). Senate Democrats choose a leader Dec. 1, with the Hill counting 15 public Schumer backers to five for Van Hollen (The Hill, Axios). In the Gulf, Iran says three tankers hit mines, and the U.S. widened sanctions (CNBC, CNN). **The October PCE report lands Wednesday at 8:30 a.m. ET** with traders pricing about a 96% chance of a December hike (Fox Business, CNBC). In engineering, investigators reproduced the router overload behind the FAA ground stop but still lack a root cause (CNBC, CNN).

markets.wrap: Stocks cooled **after Monday's best day since April 2025**. The S&P 500 slipped 0.50% and the Nasdaq fell 1.48%, while the Dow gained 0.85% (CNBC, NBC News). Nvidia fell 5.86% after Monday's 31.5% jump, and Micron, AMD, Marvell and Arm each dropped 8% to 11% (CNBC). Reports of coming tariffs on dozens of countries weighed on sentiment, citing the Wall Street Journal (CNBC). **Anthropic closed below its IPO price**, and traders now watch Wednesday's PCE inflation report (CNBC, Fox Business).

stories.title: Nvidia's Huang faces a Dec. 3 Senate hearing as both parties question his return
stories.summary: Senate Banking set a Dec. 3 hearing with Jensen Huang as the only witness, while lawmakers in both parties question the board's reinstatement.
story: Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia CEO on Monday, Nov. 23, 11 days after he resigned. Senate Banking Chairman Tim Scott has set a Dec. 3 hearing at 10 a.m. ET with Huang as the only witness, titled on export-control oversight (CNBC, The Hill). Trump told CNBC he persuaded the board to bring Huang back and said the Justice Department found no evidence of unlawful conduct by him (Fox News). The stock jumped 31% Monday, then fell 5.86% Tuesday (CNBC).

Huang resigned Nov. 12 after acknowledging an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, a company that U.S. officials are investigating. Fox News and the Washington Examiner report the administration put Megaspeed on a trade blacklist. A law enforcement source told the Examiner the Megaspeed and Super Micro inquiries are still going strong. Nvidia's board hired the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz for an independent review, and a shareholder class action is pending (CNBC).

Criticism crosses party lines. Sen. Tom Cotton called the matter the tip of the iceberg, Sen. John Curtis asked what changed while the board's own review continues, and Sen. Rick Scott said Trump's involvement looks terrible on its face (Fox News, Washington Examiner). Sen. Elizabeth Warren called the reinstatement reckless, Sen. Chuck Schumer called Trump's handling a dereliction of duty, and Rep. Hakeem Jeffries promised a probe of Nvidia and Commerce (Fox News). Attorney General Blanche and the FBI's Patel dodged questions about the case on Tuesday (CNBC).
The hearing will test whether the White House's role in the reinstatement and its China chip policy hold up under questioning from its own party.
facts: Huang resigned Nov. 12 and was reinstated Nov. 23 (Fox News, CNBC).
Senate Banking set Huang's testimony for Dec. 3 at 10 a.m. ET (CNBC).
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to testify, but no final date is confirmed (CNBC).
A shareholder class action and a board-commissioned outside review are both open (CNBC).
Megaspeed was added to a U.S. trade blacklist (Washington Examiner).
stories.next: Huang testifies Dec. 3 at 10 a.m. ET; watch whether Lutnick's date is set and whether the board's outside review reports.
stories.left: Progressives say this is a national security scandal that the White House is trying to bury. The board reversed itself while its own investigation was unfinished, and Trump said he lobbied for the outcome. They want Lutnick and Commerce to explain what they knew about Huang's ties and why export-control loopholes remain open. Warren wants answers on compliance with export rules before anyone declares the matter closed.
stories.right: Conservative critics say the reinstatement looks like favoritism for a well-connected CEO, the kind of cronyism Republicans attack Democrats for. National security hawks such as Cotton argue that a company at the center of the chip race with China should not be run by someone exposed to a suspected spy until the investigations finish. Others note the DOJ has not charged Huang and warn against a political show trial of the industry's leading firm.

stories.title: Schumer and Van Hollen head to a secret-ballot vote for Senate Democratic leader
stories.summary: The Hill counts 15 public backers for Schumer and five for Van Hollen, with 28 votes needed and most senators undeclared.
story: Senate Democrats vote Dec. 1 by secret ballot on whether Sen. Chuck Schumer stays leader or Sen. Chris Van Hollen replaces him. A candidate needs 28 votes. The Hill's whip list counts 15 senators publicly backing Schumer and five backing Van Hollen, and Axios counts 14 and five. The Hill says 34 Democratic senators have not declared (The Hill, Axios). It is the first contested race for the post since 1994, Fox News reports.

Sens. Bernie Sanders and Jeff Merkley and incoming Sens. Abdul El-Sayed and Peggy Flanagan back Van Hollen, and Sen. Elissa Slotkin switched to him after saying she would not support Schumer (The Hill). Schumer's public backers include Angela Alsobrooks, Tammy Baldwin, Catherine Cortez Masto, John Fetterman, Ruben Gallego, Jacky Rosen and Brian Schatz. Alsobrooks is from Van Hollen's home state. Fox News reports that Indivisible, MoveOn and the Working Families Party oppose Schumer.

Van Hollen has called himself the underdog but says his support is north of 15 and momentum is his, a claim the reporting has not verified (The Hill). He argues Schumer sided with the crypto industry and AIPAC against progressive candidates and says he would end the filibuster (Fox News). Schumer says he has the votes, and Democratic campaign chair Kirsten Gillibrand credited him with Democratic gains this cycle (Fox News). Trump has also attacked Schumer over his age (The Hill).
facts: The vote is Dec. 1 by secret ballot (The Hill, Axios).
28 votes are needed to win if every eligible Democrat votes (The Hill, Axios).
The Hill's whip list: 15 for Schumer, five for Van Hollen.
Van Hollen wants to end the filibuster (Fox News).
It is the first contested Democratic leader race since 1994 (Fox News).
stories.next: Dec. 1 caucus vote; watch whether Warren, Murray, Heinrich and Wyden declare before then.
stories.left: Van Hollen's supporters say the party's voters want a fighter and that Schumer's record on crypto money, Israel policy and shutdown fights has cost trust. They back changing Senate rules, including the filibuster, so a Democratic majority can pass its agenda. Schumer's defenders answer that he helped deliver pickups this cycle and that a leadership fight now wastes momentum before a new majority.
stories.right: Conservative commentators see a party arguing over how far left to move. They note Van Hollen's call to end the filibuster would remove the main check on a future Democratic majority, and that Republicans would use the same rule change later. Some also point out that Democrats are replacing an aging leader because of electoral anger from their own base, not because of any shift in ideas.

stories.title: Trump attacks Newsom's death-row commutations as 29 DAs ask the state court to stop them
stories.summary: Prosecutors from 29 counties petitioned the California Supreme Court Monday, and Newsom's reply is due Dec. 4.
story: Gov. Gavin Newsom said Nov. 5 he would commute all 548 California death sentences to life without parole. On Monday, Trump used a Justice Department event to call it one of the most shocking acts of injustice the country has seen, and he announced a federal directive to seek the death penalty in some child-murder cases and in cases where rapists or traffickers kill victims (CNN, Washington Examiner). Prosecutors from 29 counties asked the California Supreme Court Monday to halt the commutations (CalMatters).

The governor's office says 382 of the cases involve prisoners with more than one felony conviction, so four of seven justices must approve those commutations. The Criminal Justice Legal Foundation filed a separate petition. Trump has no power to reverse a state commutation, and his federal directive does not affect these cases (CNN). Several district attorneys, including in Los Angeles, Riverside and Orange counties, say they will keep seeking death sentences where the law allows (CalMatters).

Newsom wrote that the inmates will die in prison but not by our hand, and his office said Trump has used pardons to help wealthy allies (CNN, CalMatters). Critics cite voters rejecting abolition in 2012 and 2016. Los Angeles DA Nathan Hochman said the power to commute does not extend to ending the death penalty, which only the Legislature or voters can do (Fox News). Newsom's response to the court is due Dec. 4, and one report expects a ruling before he leaves office in January (CalMatters).
facts: 548 sentences are covered by the commutations (CalMatters, CNN).
The state court must approve 382 of them, needing four of seven justices.
Prosecutors from 29 counties filed Monday asking the court to halt them (CalMatters).
Trump's federal death penalty directive does not touch the state cases (CNN).
Newsom's response is due Dec. 4.
stories.next: Newsom's response is due Dec. 4; a state Supreme Court ruling could come before he leaves office in January.
stories.left: Supporters, including the ACLU and Amnesty International, say the death penalty in California is slow, costly and risks executing innocent people, and that clemency exists for this purpose. Newsom says partial relief would have created two classes of murder victims. They note the prisoners stay in prison for life and that Trump has no authority over a state's clemency.
stories.right: Critics say a governor cannot erase a punishment voters kept in 2012 and 2016, and that only the Legislature or voters can abolish it. Prosecutors object that victims' families were not heard first and that one blanket order replaces hundreds of individual judgments. Many conservatives also see a politically timed move by a likely 2028 candidate.

stories.title: San Francisco breaks its November tide record as a storm arrives with Thanksgiving travel
stories.summary: A tide of 8.23 feet topped the November record Tuesday, with a higher peak forecast near 11 a.m. Wednesday.
story: San Francisco's water level reached 8.23 feet around 10 a.m. Tuesday, breaking the November record of 7.97 feet set Nov. 30, 1982, the National Weather Service said (KQED). Forecasters expect an 8.5-foot peak shortly before 11 a.m. Wednesday, inches below the all-time January 1983 record, which CNN puts at 8.82 feet and the Chronicle at 8.66 feet. A coastal flood warning runs through Thanksgiving Day (CNN, SF Chronicle).

The tides are the highest of the season, driven by an El Niño and the peak of an 18-year lunar cycle, and a cold front adds surge (CNN, SF Chronicle). Rain forecasts have shrunk: the Chronicle now expects 0.5 to 1 inch for most of the Bay Area and 1 to 2 inches in the North Bay, mostly overnight Tuesday into Wednesday, with 30 to 40 mph gusts. Mayor Daniel Lurie urged people to avoid nonessential travel through Wednesday afternoon.

SFO no longer expects flooding to force ground stops, the Chronicle reports. The Chronicle also reports a swimmer missing at Ocean Beach after a wave pulled them under, and a Sausalito ceramics factory pushed to the brink by flooding. More king tides are expected at Christmas and in January (SF Chronicle). In Fremont, the forecast shows rain Wednesday with a 49% chance, a high of 62 and a low of 50.
facts: Tuesday's 8.23-foot tide broke the November record of 7.97 feet from 1982 (KQED).
Wednesday's peak is forecast near 8.5 feet shortly before 11 a.m.
A coastal flood warning runs through Thanksgiving Day (CNN).
Most of the Bay Area should get 0.5 to 1 inch of rain, the North Bay 1 to 2 inches (SF Chronicle).
Lurie asked residents to avoid nonessential travel through Wednesday afternoon (SF Chronicle).
stories.next: Wednesday's peak near 11 a.m., then more king tides at Christmas and in January.
stories.why: Shoreline flooding of this kind is the sort of event Bay Area planners expect to become more common with sea-level rise, and it hits roads, rail and airports at the busiest travel time of the year.

stories.title: Analyst warns a stock-market bust could open a $35 billion hole in California's budget
stories.summary: The Legislative Analyst projects a $2 billion gap in 2027-28 if markets slow, rising to $35 billion in 2028-29 after a crash.
story: California's Legislative Analyst's Office projects a small $2 billion shortfall by the end of fiscal 2027-28 if the stock market slows next year, growing to about $15 billion in 2028-29. An abrupt crash in 2027 could push the annual deficit to about $35 billion in 2028-29, and the state would lack reserves to cover it (CalMatters). KQED reports that Xavier Becerra inherits the shortfall.

The state's income tax leans on high earners whose income follows the market, so revenue swings with equities (CalMatters). That ties the budget to the same AI-driven stock rally that sold off in recent weeks. The governor's finance department has called a market downturn one of the top risks.

The analysts' warning lands as the Nasdaq sits well below its October highs after the Nvidia selloff, though Monday's rebound was the best session since April 2025 (CNBC). Republicans hold only about one in six seats in the Legislature, so Democrats own both the problem and the fixes (CalMatters).
facts: The LAO sees a $2 billion gap by 2027-28 if markets slow (CalMatters).
The gap could reach $15 billion in 2028-29.
An abrupt 2027 crash could mean about $35 billion a year by 2028-29, with no reserves to cover it.
California's income tax relies heavily on high earners tied to the market.
stories.next: The governor's January budget proposal will show how much market risk the state builds in.
stories.blindspot: Found coverage from CalMatters and KQED only; no right-leaning outlet reported on this outlook.
stories.left: Progressives argue the state should diversify revenue instead of relying on top earners, and that deep cuts to health care and schools in a downturn would hit the poor first. Many favor higher taxes on wealth and corporations and bigger rainy-day reserves.
stories.right: Conservatives say the forecast proves Sacramento spent as if the AI boom would last forever. They want spending restraint and budget rules that bank windfalls, and they warn that higher taxes on high earners would drive them out of state and worsen the volatility.

stories.title: Iran says three tankers hit mines as the U.S. widens sanctions and talks stay stalled
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says three tankers hit mines in Hormuz despite U.S. escorts, while Washington sanctions more Iranian networks.
story: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says three oil tankers suffered a severe explosion and fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz despite U.S. escorts, and the Treasury widened sanctions on more than two dozen Iranian exchange houses, front companies and people (CNBC). Iran's mine claims are often unverified. CNN reports attacks in and around the strait are at their highest level since the war began, with at least 22 in November as of Sunday.

The U.S. maintains a naval blockade of Iranian ports and added a third carrier, the USS Theodore Roosevelt, to the Gulf last week (CNBC). Fox News reports Iran has staged 14 tankers at Kharg Island to try to run the blockade, and Trump dared Tehran to try, saying the ships would end up at the bottom of the sea. A maritime security expert called the convoy plan farcical.

Diplomacy looks stalled. Trump said the U.S. does not need a deal with Iran, while Iran's foreign minister says Tehran remains open to a broader settlement if the blockade ends, sanctions are lifted in steps and frozen funds are released (CNBC). WTI crude settled at $81.41, up 1.55%, after a roughly 4% drop Monday (live.json, CNBC).
facts: Iran's Guards say three tankers hit mines despite U.S. escorts (CNBC).
At least 22 attacks near the strait were reported in November as of Sunday (CNN).
The U.S. added a third aircraft carrier last week (CNBC).
New Treasury sanctions hit more than two dozen Iranian entities and people (CNBC).
WTI crude closed at $81.41, up 1.55% (live.json).
stories.next: Whether the reported 14-tanker convoy tries to leave Kharg; watch oil before Thanksgiving's thin trading.
stories.left: Progressives say the war has no clear exit: a blockade, more sanctions and a third carrier raise the odds of a miscalculation while diplomacy sits idle. They point to inflation driven by energy prices and say Congress should demand an end-state plan and a vote on continued operations.
stories.right: Conservatives say pressure is working: no Iranian tanker has broken the blockade, and Tehran's mine and convoy claims are bluster. They argue talks follow strength, and that rushing a deal now would reward Iran's attacks on shipping and leave its nuclear question unresolved.

stories.title: Traders see a December Fed hike as locked in as the PCE report arrives Wednesday
stories.summary: CME FedWatch shows about a 96% chance of a quarter-point hike Dec. 9; Waller has floated a half-point.
story: Traders put the probability of a quarter-point Fed hike at the Dec. 8-9 meeting at about 96%, according to CME FedWatch, as cited by Fox Business. The October PCE inflation report is due Wednesday at 8:30 a.m. ET, the last major inflation reading before the meeting (CNBC, Fox Business). The 10-year Treasury yield sat at 4.90% on Tuesday (live.json).

Inflation has run hot. October CPI came in above forecasts, and October wholesale inflation reached 6.5% a year, the largest since November 2022 (CNBC). September headline PCE rose to 3.6% and core PCE to 3.1% (Fox Business). The Fed began hiking in September for the first time since 2023, and Chair Kevin Warsh has said it is the Fed's responsibility to get inflation down.
Fed Governor Christopher Waller has hinted at a bigger, half-point hike (Washington Examiner).  Bill Ackman, on Fox Business, warned that further hikes risk a recession.
facts: About 96% odds of a quarter-point hike Dec. 9 (Fox Business, CME FedWatch).
October PCE is due Wednesday at 8:30 a.m. ET.
September PCE: headline 3.6%, core 3.1% (Fox Business).
October wholesale inflation ran 6.5% a year (CNBC).
The 10-year Treasury yield was 4.90% Tuesday (live.json).
stories.next: Wednesday's PCE print at 8:30 a.m. ET, then the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting.
stories.left: Progressives worry rate hikes aimed at energy-driven inflation will cost jobs while doing little about oil shocks from the Iran war. They argue tariffs and war spending are feeding prices, so the Fed is being asked to clean up policy made elsewhere.
stories.right: Conservatives say inflation of 3.6% and rising wholesale prices show the Fed was late and must keep tightening. They fault tariffs and spending for pressure on prices, and argue that credibility requires finishing the job even if markets wobble, as Chair Warsh has indicated.

stories.title: Nvidia gives back part of its record rally and chip stocks drop sharply
stories.summary: Nvidia fell 5.86% Tuesday after Monday's 31.5% jump, dragging the Nasdaq down 1.48% while the Dow rose.
story: Wall Street's Monday rally cooled Tuesday. The S&P 500 fell 0.50% to 7,201.09 and the Nasdaq lost 1.48% to 23,733.53, while the Dow rose 0.85% to 50,018.70 (live.json, CNBC, NBC News). Nvidia fell 5.86% to $155.38 after its record one-day gain, which came when its board brought Jensen Huang back (CNBC).

Chip stocks took the brunt. CNBC reports Micron dropped 10.97%, AMD 8.86%, Marvell 9.10% and Arm 8.55%. Nvidia is still down about 30% from its Oct. 6 record, and one Wolfe Research note put the semiconductor ETF more than 42% below its June high (CNBC). Of the other tracked names, Apple rose 1.43% to $354.07 and Microsoft rose 0.74% to $496.13, while Alphabet fell 1.08%, Amazon 1.21% and Tesla 0.20%.

Reports that the administration is preparing to raise tariffs on dozens of countries, including China, weighed on sentiment, citing the Wall Street Journal (CNBC live blog). Crude rose 1.55% to $81.41, Bitcoin fell 2.57% to $59,639, and the 10-year yield eased to 4.90% (live.json). Anthropic closed below its IPO price (CNBC).
facts: Nvidia fell 5.86% to $155.38 after a 31.5% gain Monday (CNBC).
Micron fell 10.97%, AMD 8.86%, Marvell 9.10% and Arm 8.55% (CNBC).
Nvidia remains about 30% below its Oct. 6 record (CNBC).
Markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving (CNBC).
stories.next: PCE inflation Wednesday morning; U.S. markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving.
stories.why: Nvidia's whiplash shows how much of the market's value rides on one company and one executive, and the chip rout suggests Monday's rebound has not settled doubts about AI spending or the Huang investigations.

stories.title: FAA pauses router upgrades as investigators reproduce the overload behind the Nov. 13 ground stop
stories.summary: Investigators have reproduced a network overload tied to an Arkansas router, but the root cause is still unknown.
story: The Nov. 13 ground stop lasted more than four hours and affected 17 of 22 en route control centers. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blames a router installed in El Dorado, Arkansas, which flooded other systems with connection attempts. The FAA paused new router installations Nov. 17 and disabled the same function on more than 60 other Juniper routers (CNN, CNBC). Engineers have reproduced the network overload, but no definitive cause is established (CNBC).

The router was installed by L3Harris, the FAA's prime contractor, during a copper-to-fiber upgrade. A second router in Amarillo, Texas also showed problems. HPE, which owns Juniper, says the equipment worked as configured, and the FAA says an FAA technician watched the installation (CNN, Axios). The FBI has taken possession of the device and officials see no sign of a cyberattack.

Democratic senators on the Commerce Committee wrote that identifying the failed device does not explain why it failed, and asked the FAA, L3Harris and Juniper for a briefing (CNBC, Axios). IEEE Spectrum puts the outage in a wider pattern of critical-system crashes, and Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton has called recent outages unconnected, not a coordinated attack (IEEE Spectrum, CNBC).
facts: The ground stop affected 17 of 22 en route centers (CNN).
The FAA paused router installs and disabled the function on 60+ other routers (CNN, CNBC).
Engineers reproduced the overload, but the root cause is not established (CNBC).
HPE says Juniper's equipment worked as configured (CNN).
The FBI has the router; officials report no sign of a cyberattack (CNN, CNBC).
stories.next: A root-cause finding from the FAA, L3Harris and Juniper; senators sought a briefing from them.
stories.why: A single misbehaving network device took down most of the country's en route air traffic centers, which points to weak fault isolation in a system that is being modernized one site at a time.

stories.title: Engineers pitch 800-volt DC and batteries to tame AI data centers' grid-shaking power swings
stories.summary: AI training loads can swing by hundreds of megawatts several times a second, and vendors say DC distribution and batteries can absorb it.
story: IEEE Spectrum reports that AI data center loads can swing from near zero to hundreds of megawatts and back several times per second, a pattern the grid was not built for. Dimaag's vice president of business development says battery and control software between the grid and the data center can isolate those swings (IEEE Spectrum). ON.energy's CTO warns that 1-gigawatt swings several times per minute could cause frequency problems.

In 800 VDC designs, grid power is converted to direct current at the site perimeter, replacing several conversion steps. IEEE Spectrum reports the shift from 415-volt AC to 800-volt DC lets about 85% more power flow through the same conductor size. Nvidia expects 800 VDC facilities to begin appearing in 2027, and Spectrum notes Texas, despite its solar, wind and batteries, is far from ready for them.

Regulators are catching up. Under NERC's new rules, data centers of at least 50 megawatts connected at 100 kilovolts or above must give grid operators detailed models of how they draw power (IEEE Spectrum). The performance claims here come from simulations and vendors, not field deployments.
facts: Loads can swing from near zero to hundreds of megawatts several times a second (IEEE Spectrum).
800 VDC distribution is said to carry 85% more power through the same conductors than 415 VAC.
Nvidia expects 800 VDC facilities from 2027.
NERC requires load models from data centers of 50 MW or more at 100 kV or above.
stories.next: Nvidia's 2027 800 VDC timeline and how grid operators apply NERC's rules.
stories.flag: Performance figures come from simulations and company statements, not independent field data.
stories.why: Grid connection and power quality, not chips alone, are becoming the constraint on AI build-outs, so power electronics and storage are now part of the AI hardware stack.

stories.title: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth but has sent no science data since Nov. 14
stories.summary: NASA says the probe reached about 16 billion miles on Nov. 18 and still transmits a carrier signal.
story: NASA says Voyager 1 reached one light-day from Earth on Nov. 18, about 16 billion miles, after more than 49 years of travel. The team noticed Nov. 14 that the spacecraft had stopped sending science and engineering data, though it still transmits a carrier signal (NASA, Nature, Space.com).

The carrier signal shows the spacecraft's attitude control computer is keeping the antenna pointed at Earth and the transmitter is working. The team says the lack of data points to the onboard computer that gathers and formats instrument data, not to the antenna (NASA). A similar episode in 2023 was caused by one of the onboard computers.

Project manager Suzanne Dodd said any diagnosis takes about two days because of the round-trip signal delay and low data rates, and the team expects a fix (Space.com). Voyager 1 has been in interstellar space and is humanity's farthest spacecraft.
facts: Voyager 1 reached one light-day from Earth on Nov. 18 (NASA).
It is about 16 billion miles away.
Science and engineering data stopped Nov. 14; a carrier signal continues (NASA).
Each diagnostic step takes about two days (Space.com).
stories.next: Engineers' next commands to the data-handling computer; each round trip takes about two days.
stories.why: The mission is still returning the only direct measurements from interstellar space, and each failure of a decades-old system limits how much longer it can.

stories.title: Gravitational-wave data hint that many merging black holes come from stars that failed to explode
stories.summary: A Physical Review D study ties a peak at 10 solar masses in merging black holes to failed supernovae.
story: A study in Physical Review D by Legred, Golomb and Chatziioannou argues that an excess of merging black holes near 10 solar masses may come from massive stars that collapsed directly without a bright explosion (Space.com, APS). Black holes near that mass make up about 75% of the sample in the press release's analysis and show a narrower range of spin speeds than the rest (Space.com).

Rates drop steeply above the peak, by roughly two orders of magnitude between masses near 10 and 15 solar masses, with a lack of black holes at 12 to 16 solar masses (APS, EurekAlert). The arXiv version analyzes 153 events from the GWTC-4.0 catalog, and the press release cites 257 mergers, a difference the coverage does not explain.

The authors say the evidence is consistent with failed supernovae but not direct proof, and such events have not been confirmed. Simulations of supernova collapse may help show why a narrow mass range collapses so efficiently.
facts: The study was published in Physical Review D (APS).
It addresses a peak near 10 solar masses in merging black holes.
Spin measurements lend some support (Space.com).
The authors call the finding consistent with, not proof of, failed supernovae.
stories.next: More gravitational-wave detections to test whether the 10-solar-mass peak and spin pattern hold.
stories.flag: Sample sizes differ between the paper (153 events) and the press release (257 mergers).
stories.why: If many black holes form without an explosion, models of how stars die and how heavy elements spread through galaxies need revising.

stories.title: Anthropic closes below its $83 IPO price in its fourth trading day
stories.summary: Shares fell 6.5% Tuesday to under $83 after a 17% debut pop, while most analysts stay positive.
story: Anthropic's stock closed down 6.5% on Tuesday, below its $83 IPO price, after four trading days (CNBC). Bloomberg reported a close of $81.91. It priced Nov. 18, selling 980 million shares to raise about $81.3 billion, the largest IPO on record, then opened at $111.50 and closed its first day at $97.17 (CNBC, TechCrunch). It took four days to break the offer price, versus 21 trading days for SpaceX.

Analysts remain mostly positive: six of seven covering the stock rate it buy or strong buy, per LSEG data. Canaccord has a $135 target, Oppenheimer $150 and Wedbush $120. Seaport is neutral and cautious on revenue growth (CNBC).

Options volume surged, with nearly 500,000 contracts by noon ET and puts outnumbering calls. The largest trade was a $7.5 million purchase of 75-strike puts expiring in mid-December, a bet on another 11% drop. Another large trade bet on a 19% rally within two months (CNBC). Axios has questioned the tension between investors' faith in rapid AI progress and the company's own risk disclosures.
facts: Anthropic priced at $83 on Nov. 18 and raised about $81.3 billion (CNBC).
It closed down 6.5% Tuesday, below the offer price (CNBC).
Debut: opened at $111.50, closed at $97.17 on Nov. 19.
Six of seven analysts rate it buy or strong buy (LSEG via CNBC).
stories.next: Mid-December option expiries, including the $75 puts, and any further analyst initiations.
stories.flag: Sources differ on the closing price: CNBC reports a 6.5% drop; Bloomberg reported $81.91.
stories.why: A fast drop through the offer price shows how quickly sentiment toward AI leaders has turned, and it adds to the pressure on the AI trade that sold off earlier this month. Anthropic makes Claude, the assistant writing this briefing.

stories.title: Axios: AI is speeding up, partly because AI is helping build AI
stories.summary: Axios reports METR finds model progress at nearly twice the historical pace, with AI doing a growing share of research.
story: Axios reports that independent researchers at METR found AI models advancing at nearly twice their historical pace, driven in part by AI itself, with no clear obstacle to sustaining that over the next year (Axios). It cites Anthropic data showing Claude's share of company AI research tasks rose from under 1% in February to more than a quarter by August, with humans still supervising.

The AI Futures Project now expects machines to surpass top human AI researchers next year, and Paul Christiano puts one-in-three odds on superintelligence within a year at the current pace (Axios). A companion Axios column says Anthropic's amended S-1 states it may imminently cross its own threshold for AI-driven acceleration but has not yet done so.

Axios also reports that OpenAI disclosed Astra 6.2 is its first publicly released model to reach its High threshold for AI self-improvement, which OpenAI likens to giving each researcher another capable engineer. Only Axios has reported the Astra 6.2 claim.
facts: METR reportedly sees AI progress at nearly twice its historical pace (Axios).
Claude's share of Anthropic's AI research tasks rose from under 1% to over a quarter by August (Axios).
OpenAI reportedly rated Astra 6.2 High for self-improvement (Axios, single source).
Anthropic's S-1 says it may imminently cross its acceleration threshold (Axios).
stories.next: Whether OpenAI or Anthropic publishes details of their self-improvement thresholds, and METR's next update.
stories.flag: Figures are Axios's characterizations of METR, company data and the S-1; the Astra 6.2 claim has no second source or OpenAI primary source.
stories.why: If AI is doing a large part of AI research, forecasts and safety plans built around human-paced progress may be out of date, and the claims here shape how investors price the labs.

stories.title: Google's Gemini can now operate a Mac and make calls and purchases for you
stories.summary: Gemini's Mac app added computer use, and Tasks, which can book appointments and buy things, is free to Gemini 4 Hydrogen users.
story: Google added computer use to the Gemini Mac app Nov. 19. The agent can navigate native Mac apps and browse websites in the background while the user's screen and cursor stay free, and users can pause or approve actions (TechCrunch). The feature is in English in the U.S. and needs a Google AI Plus, Pro or Ultra subscription.

On Nov. 17, Google made Tasks, which can call businesses, book appointments, buy things with Google Pay and sign into sites when prompted, available for free to hundreds of millions of people using Gemini 4 Hydrogen (TechCrunch). Hydrogen, released Nov. 12, is a fast model built for agentic work and is rolling out to Search, the Gemini API and AI Studio.

Google's frontier models, Gemini 4 Carbon and Argon, remain aimed at deep reasoning (TechCrunch). CNBC reported in October that Google was pushing a Gemini agent for work as Wall Street shifted attention to personal agents.
facts: Mac computer use launched Nov. 19 for paid subscribers in the U.S. (TechCrunch).
Tasks is free with Gemini 4 Hydrogen (TechCrunch).
Users can pause and approve agent actions.
Hydrogen is rolling out to Search and the Gemini API (TechCrunch).
stories.next: Expansion beyond English and the U.S., and any security reviews of agents that sign into accounts.
stories.why: Agents that act inside your accounts move AI from answering questions to doing errands, which raises the stakes for permissions, fraud and mistakes.

stories.title: An early flu season and measles surge arrive as the CDC stays quiet
stories.summary: CNN reports about 3.7 million flu infections so far, and the U.S. has lost measles elimination status.
story: An early flu season has caught many Americans unprotected. CDC data cited by CNN show about 3.7 million infections, 50,000 hospitalizations and 2,800 deaths so far, with about half of states reporting moderate to high activity, mostly in the South and West. Vaccination is lagging: about 32% of children and teens, 29% of pregnant women and 37% of adults (CNN).

The U.S. officially lost its measles elimination status this month (NPR, NBC News). The CDC counts 5,838 confirmed cases this year through Nov. 19, with Pennsylvania at 1,529, by far the most (Axios). Deaths are reported as 11 by CNN and 10 by NPR.

CDC Director Erica Schwartz has stressed vaccination and the agency says it put $100 million into state and local health departments. Critics say the agency has been quiet on flu. Measles typically peaks in late winter and early spring, which can overlap with flu season (CNN).
facts: About 3.7 million flu infections, 50,000 hospitalizations and 2,800 deaths so far (CNN).
The U.S. lost measles elimination status (NPR, NBC News).
5,838 measles cases through Nov. 19; Pennsylvania has 1,529 (Axios).
Flu vaccination: 32% of children, 29% of pregnant women, 37% of adults (CNN).
stories.next: Next CDC flu update and measles counts; both seasons tend to peak in winter.
stories.why: Holiday travel and gatherings spread both viruses, and low vaccination rates mean outbreaks can grow faster than hospitals plan for.

briefs: CIA and ODNI suffered an apparent hack of an open-source intelligence system that affected unclassified information, four sources told CNN; the cause and timing are unclear.
Jensen Huang told staff at his first all-hands since returning that Nvidia does not need a succession plan (CNBC).
Astronomers found a rare triple star system, a red dwarf and two white dwarfs, about 28 light-years away (Space.com).
NASA's Chandra identified a hidden companion pulling material from a massive star every 113 days (NASA Science).
WSJ-sourced reports of coming tariff increases on dozens of countries, including China, weighed on stocks Monday, according to CNBC's live blog.
